talks.title: Congreso de Hackers - Security Conference 2022
talks.teaser: Analyzes congreso de Hackers - Security Conference 2022 and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
This long broadcast from the Dragonheart security congress, held online in 2022, strings together several sessions from a multi-day event, with opening remarks, sponsor mentions and CTF announcements. The first session is an introduction to smart contract security in Web3. The speaker explains how blockchain networks, wallets and contract deployment work, then covers reentrancy, where a withdraw function sends funds before updating balances so an attacker can drain a contract through repeated calls. A second example shows an auction contract frozen by a bidder whose refund is rejected. Mitigations discussed include updating state before external calls and adding locks. The session also covers tx.origin authorization flaws and phishing through malicious token approvals, with a demonstration that ends before the full attack is shown.

The next session walks through analysing malicious network traffic in Wireshark. It shows how to build a custom profile with useful columns, filter HTTP and TLS server names, and identify hosts and Windows users through DHCP, NetBIOS and Kerberos traffic. The speaker then traces a campaign from a sample capture, including exporting a suspicious file for hash lookup, and notes that widespread encryption makes this work harder.

A session on open-source intelligence and pretexting describes how company registries, professional networking sites and email-finder services can build a target profile. A phone pretext moves from a receptionist to a director and secures a meeting, and the speaker urges people to limit technology details shared online and to avoid giving out phone numbers.

The final session presents research into video surveillance cameras from a major vendor, where exposed cloud services allowed device data to be extracted. The speaker grades sabotage and intrusion techniques from physical tampering to cloud data extraction. The recording ends before the demonstration.
